chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: NBC Merchandise Mart with Jules Herbuveaux; the Wingy Manone show
summary: Whiteman puts him on staff with Jules Herbuveaux's group and he also leads an early-morning jazz show with Wingy Manone, Volly De Faut and Dave Rose.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: At NBC -- that's the Merchandise Mart, now it was open.
So, we were like the Blue Blazers in the afternoon, we're the Tea -- I mean the morning, the Blue Blazers in the afternoon. --
Well he'd seen me and the people over there, because prior to this time, when I was with Victor Young -

On that show, a few months before, I'd met a bunch of guys, I knew all the jazz guys in Chicago, they begin to know me and know that I was playing that way. So I got a show with Wingy Manone, Volly Faux Defoe --
Yeah, Volly -- well he was a Chicago kid. He came --
But He had that sound -- didn't he have that clarinet -- that New Orleans kind of sound?
Well, I don't know. He was a good clarinet player. He was -- like Chicago style playing --
I doubt New Orleans -- I don't he he --
-- no, he didn't. He was a good clarinet player. He was like --
Well didn't he play an Albert or something?
Yeah, I think he did. He was considered one of the best --
And, Dave Rose was the piano player.
And we used to -- will you believe this?

We used to do a program, an hour from 7:00 to 8:00 in the morning, one a week. So I had two shows. I had Victor's and I had this. And I was the leader of that show. So, they used to come in -- people used to come in and listen --
Yeah, now -- that's at the Merchandise Mart, NBC --
